Here is the schema: https://gist.github.com/AFDudley/16b4de251adf31b38bc6e2932bac5d64 I can grab a license for KDB+ up to 128cores for free https://github.com/sambacha/orderbook-data-raw any sort of estimate on how many gigs we are talking not entirely sure because there is a very large dataset that i'm not granting access to, i'd expect 100s of MB a day. because it's a test database there are large gaps, but it's been running for over a year. postgres? yes you want to try kdb+? they have a whitepaper on this https://code.kx.com/q/wp/transaction-cost/ Do you mean do I want to migrate my TBs of data sitting in SAN to a new database? hahahaha not quite i barely have the patience for a 200mb excel file Sorry, it's only 712GB at the moment. that gist is everything in their correct? no. i'm trying to guestimate what the size for you would be... my intuition tells me there just isn't a lot of the type of data you asked for though. There aren't even a 100 people doing PGAs, so... I already accepted that fact so I am trying to replicate it based of SPY ticks and orders and approximate it onto eth? maybe? alot of assumptions Yeah, that's not a great way of doing it. yeah i know 1. eth transactions vary significantly in size they aren't like ticks at all. technically it's timeseries data, but that's about where the similarities end. it be more akin to a physical commodity like electricity than SPY consumption of product *meaning* relatively soon, similar to gas transaction pricing most transactions are mined relatively soon after "purchase" yeah, i'm not sure how this reasoning by analogy helps in this case. especially given "auction theory" is a thing. it doesnt if , as you said the data doesn;t substantiate the claim that the orderbook data is similar it's nothing like orderbook data. even thinking about it as an auction is dangerous since not every transaction is really participating yeah , its not a metaphor for a reason 😛 100% right you could say tho, that transaction settlement time does have a play in traditional capital markets, but to the extent you would see that solely off tick data etc, you would need to know who was placing what, when but ya , distraction
